items.excerpt: Anthony Wilson Blindfold Test — guitarist reacts to tracks by Julian Lage, Ben Monder, Mary Halvorson, and others.
items.body:
Blindfold Test: Anthony Wilson

About Anthony Wilson
- Grammy-nominated guitarist and arranger who rose to notoriety in 1997 with his self-titled debut
- Longtime guitarist for Diana Krall
- Released critically acclaimed nonet albums
- Returned to the nonet format in 2025 with House Of The Singing Blossoms (Sam First)

Selections:
1. Julian Lage — "Ocala" from Scenes From Above (Blue Note, 2026)
2. Jimmy Smith/Wes Montgomery — "13 (Death March)" from Jimmy & Wes: The Dynamic Duo (Verve, 1966)
3. Alan Ferber Nonet — "Luteous Pangolin" from The Compass (Fresh Sound New Talent, 2008)
4. Miles Okazaki — "Skippy" from Work–The Complete Recordings Of Thelonious Monk (2018)
5. Andrew Renfroe — "Big Country" from Pop Logic (2025)
6. Ben Monder — "Where Or When" from Planetarium (Sunnyside, 2024)
7. Mary Halvorson — "About Ghosts" from About Ghosts (Nonesuch, 2025)

items.excerpt: New Orleans-raised alto saxophonist Jesse Davis, 40 years into his career, reflects on his journey following his 60th birthday with a new album, Reflections (Cellar Music).
items.body:
Jesse Davis Rediscovers Joy

New Orleans-raised alto saxophonist Jesse Davis, 40 years into his career, reflects on his journey following his 60th birthday with a new album, Reflections (Cellar Music). The album represents a homecoming — both musically and personally — as Davis reconnects with the joy of playing jazz.

Quote: "Forty years into this career, I have come back to myself, and I feel the same joy I did the first time I opened that sax case every time I play."

Albums as bandleader: 10. Key collaborators: Clark Terry, Ray Brown, Milt Jackson, Benny Golson. 1980s prominence as part of the "young lions" movement spearheaded by Wynton Marsalis.

The Album: Reflections (Cellar Music)
- "Blue Autumn" — sprightly, Latin-influenced opener exploring grief
- "Choctaw Alley" — blues-inflected, evokes New Orleans roots
- "Reflections" — Monk standard
- "Evidence" — Monk standard

Musicians: Jesse Davis (alto sax), Spike Wilner (piano), John Webber (bass), Lewis Nash (drums)

items.excerpt: Profile of Kabir Sehgal — former finance executive turned 14-time Grammy-winning music producer and creator, pivoting toward personal creative work in meditative music.
items.body:
Kabir Sehgal's Community of Curiosity

Profile of Kabir Sehgal — a former finance executive turned prolific Grammy-winning music producer and creator. On Feb. 1, Sehgal received his 14th Grammy Award as producer of the audiobook Meditations: The Reflections Of His Holiness The Dalai Lama.

Notable collaborators: Ted Nash, Joe Alterman, Rufus Wainwright, Maggie Rogers, Andra Day, Arturo O'Farrill, Jonathan Batiste, Lil Jon.

Latest Release: stars and static — 10-track, 30-minute lo-fi digital meditation combining field recordings of American locales with iconic American songs.

Career: Vice president of emerging markets at J.P. Morgan, published 4th book Coined, produced 30+ albums. Now pivoting from producer to creator.

items.excerpt: Coverage of FIMAV (Festival du Musique Actuelle de Victoriaville) — returned with new director Scott Thomson and 20+ avant-garde performances.
items.body:
Back on the Cutting-Edge Trail, in Victoriaville

Coverage of FIMAV (Festival du Musique Actuelle de Victoriaville), Quebec. The festival returned after near-absence the previous year under new director Scott Thomson.

Notable performances:
- Amirtha Kidambi's Elder Ones
- Darius Jones Trio
- Zubot Brothers (Joshua and Jesse)
- John Oswald's "PlunderphoniCoveralls"
- Queen Mab — Marilyn Lerner + Lori Freedman (40 years together)
- Pat Thomas solo piano and with أحمد [Ahmed]
- Rafael Toral (Portuguese electric guitarist)
- Sarah Pagé's Voda with No Hay Banda
- Eric Chenaux
- Fanfare Pourpour (20-piece ensemble)

The 20-piece ensemble Fanfare Pourpour, which began life as a guerilla street band in Montreal in the '70s, closed the festival.
